alex: Heads-up — nightly perf job shows a ~12% tail latency regression on the hosted path after yesterday's kernel-selection tweaks. Attaching the CI run IDs and traces.
perf-ci-bot: automated run started: perf-nightly-1805-23 (commit: 2f9c8b6). Collected: nsight(.qdrep)=s3://redwood-perf/2f9c8b6/1805001234.qdrep, perfetto(.pftrace)=s3://redwood-perf/2f9c8b6/1805001234.pftrace, kernel-timeline(.parquet)=s3://redwood-perf/2f9c8b6/1805001234.kernels.parquet
mar ia: @alex can you paste the failing query or workload (prefix lengths, batch sizes)? we should triage whether it's KV cache evictions or batching heuristic hitting a bad path.
alex: repro details — small-batch chat workload: seq_len=512, reqs/sec bursty around 200 rps, kv cache hit-rate dropped from ~92% -> ~68 at the regression window. Batching distribution shifted: more single-request microbatches.
devin: sounds like the kernel selector fell back to the slow fp32 path for the 512 token case after the recent heuristic change. I saw a similar pattern: new heur chooses fused-gemm only when avg_seq < 256.
kevin: we need a CI-side filter: only keep full traces for runs with regression >5%, otherwise store a summarized timeline. That saves S3 and speeds diffs.
maria: proposal: store two artifact tiers — full (qdrep + pftrace + raw kernels.parquet) for regressions or weekly samples; summarized (top-20 kernels + condensed perfetto slices + compressed parquet) otherwise. Use object keys with content-addressed names to dedupe: s3://redwood-perf/<commit>/<run>/<sha256-of-artifact>.zst
alex: agreed. also keep a small manifest.json next to artifacts with metrics: {"p50","p95","p99","kv_hit","batch_dist"} so dashboard can decide whether to fetch full trace.
devin: here's a quick helper to collect nsight in CI (we'll run inside the docker job):
```bash
NSYS_OUT=perf-${CI_COMMIT_SHA}_${CI_RUN_ID}.qdrep
nsys profile --sample=cpu --trace=nvtx,cuda --output ${NSYS_OUT} --force ./bin/serve-bench --args "--workload config.json"
# then convert to perfetto slice for smaller diffs
nsys export --format=sqlite ${NSYS_OUT} -o ${NSYS_OUT}.sqlite
python tools/nsys_to_perfetto.py ${NSYS_OUT}.sqlite ${NSYS_OUT}.pftrace
# zstd compress final artifacts
zstd -19 ${NSYS_OUT} -o ${NSYS_OUT}.zst
```
kevin: +1. For the dashboard diffs: convert kernel timelines to parquet with columns (kernel_name, start_ns, duration_ns, sm_eff, occupancy, bytes_loaded). Then diff by kernel_name+p90 duration. That avoids loading big qdreps.
perf-ci-bot: perf-nightly-1805-23 summary: p50 +2.3%, p95 +12.1% (regression flagged). Manifest written to s3://redwood-perf/2f9c8b6/1805001234/manifest.json. Full artifacts retained per policy.
alex: Maria/Devin, can one of you add the retention + dedupe logic to the CI job today? I can follow up with the dashboard API for selective fetching.
maria: taking it. I'll add lifecycle rules + a lambda that prunes duplicates and populates a manifest index. Will open a tiny PR.
devin: I'll add the nsight export + parquet pipeline step. Also will add a small perf regression alert that posts to this channel with the diff link: https://internal.redwood/perf/diff/2f9c8b6/1805001234
kevin: also consider compressed parquet + column projection for the web UI to keep dashboards snappy.
alex: perfect. if we can get this in today we can re-run the nightly with dedupe and a sampled-week retention and see storage drop. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
